previous_disclosures.summary: Citi has ended nearly all institutional banking services in Russia, retaining only those necessary to meet legal and regulatory obligations, while also significantly reducing its consumer loan portfolio in the region. The company has ceased soliciting new business or clients in Russia and is managing existing commitments and supporting employees during this wind-down period.

current_disclosures.summary: Citi ended nearly all institutional banking services in Russia and ceased new business solicitations, retaining only services required for legal, regulatory, and employee support obligations.
Citi significantly reduced its consumer loan portfolio in Russia through portfolio sales and a credit card referral agreement with a Russian bank.

Citi's remaining Russia operations are conducted through Services, Markets, Banking and All Other-Legacy Franchises, with ongoing monitoring of the war in Ukraine, sanctions, and economic conditions to mitigate exposures.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm continues to monitor its exposure to Russia, which consists of cash placed with the central bank excluding client deposits, and currently believes this remaining exposure is not material. Information regarding Russian litigation is referenced in Note 30.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan disclose that they continue to monitor their remaining exposure to Russia. Citi specifies that its remaining operations are conducted through specific franchises (Services, Markets, Banking, All Other-Legacy) and that it continues to mitigate exposures as appropriate. JPMorgan similarly states it monitors its exposure, defined specifically as cash placed with the central bank (excluding client deposits), and currently believes this remaining exposure is not material. Both disclosures emphasize active monitoring of residual geopolitical risks.

sentences.text: Citi continues to monitor the war in Ukraine, related sanctions and economic conditions and continues to mitigate its Russia exposures and risks as appropriate.

The Firm continues to monitor its exposure to Russia, which corresponds to cash placed with the central bank, but which excludes deposits placed on behalf of clients at the Deposit Insurance Agency of Russia.
The Firm currently believes that its remaining exposure to Russia is not material.
